title: Renewal & Expansion Check-in — Cascade Energy
summary: Quarterly renewal and expansion check-in focused on increasing Dedicated capacity, adding EU region support, and discussing contract extension options. Customer wants predictable latency for inference, regional data residency, and a procurement timeline to finalize before EOY. SE to run updated benchmark on their workload; AE to send pricing addendum and security artifacts.
topics: Dedicated capacity upgrade (more GPUs / burst capacity)
Contract term and pricing (12 vs 24 months)
next_steps: Maya to send updated pricing addendum with 24/12 month options by 2026-12-07
Carlos to run a 24-hour benchmark on Cascade sample workload and share results by 2026-12-10
Maya to share SOC 2 and network architecture docs (VPC, KMS) today
Cascade to confirm required EU regions and internal PO timeline by 2026-12-11
Schedule procurement/legal follow-up call week of 2026-12-14

Maya Thompson: prepare pricing addendum and region addendum; include burst capacity notes by 2026-12-07
Liam O'Connor: confirm EU region list (eu-west-1 vs eu-central) and data residency constraints by 2026-12-11

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-05 15:00 PST — Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Thompson (Redwood AE), Carlos Nguyen (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Head of Platform, Cascade), Priya Rao (SRE), Jared Kim (Procurement), Sara Martinez (Eng Manager)

Summary: quick renewal check-in, explore capacity upgrades and EU region add, align on procurement timing.

00:00 Maya Thompson: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time right at the end of the week. Quick roll call?
00:12 Liam O'Connor: Hey Maya, Liam here.
00:15 Priya Rao: Priya on SRE.
00:18 Jared Kim: Jared from procurement.
00:20 Sara Martinez: Sara here.
00:22 Maya Thompson: Great, Carlos is on too — Carlos, want to say hi?
00:25 Carlos Nguyen: Hey team, Carlos Nguyen, principal SE at Redwood. I'll be owning the benchmark and technical follow-ups.
00:32 Maya Thompson: Cool. High level — we wanted to talk through your renewal approach, any expansion needs, and how to get an updated dedicated capacity plan in place. You're up for renewal in January right?
00:44 Liam O'Connor: Yeah renewal window is Jan 15th. We're looking at two things mainly: more predictable throughput for our inference jobs — we have some new workloads — and adding EU regions for data residency for our clients in Dublin and Frankfurt. Also procurement wants options for 12 vs 24 month terms.
01:05 Maya Thompson: Totally. For throughput, we usually recommend bumping to a higher dedicated pool with autoscaling + a modest burst bucket. That keeps p99 latency within SLO while letting you save on steady-state. Carlos can talk about perf.
01:17 Carlos Nguyen: Sure — from the technical bench perspective, our metric is tokens per second and p99 tail latency. Based on the sample traces you shared last quarter, moving from your current 4xV100 equivalent to an 8xA100 pool should get you roughly 2.3x throughput for the prompt mix you have. There's variance — if you call long contexts frequently we need to review kv cache behavior.
01:45 Priya Rao: small note, some of our production jobs spike with long histories — we care about tail latency under 500ms for the 90th percentile, and p99 ideally under 800ms.
01:58 Carlos Nguyen: Right, we can tune batch sizes and caching. For long-context jobs we enable prefix caching and a different kernel path; that reduces per-token compute and often improves p99. We'll test using your sample prompts.
02:12 Sara Martinez: On regions — is it straightforward to add EU regions to our Dedicated deployment? We need data at rest to stay in EU.
02:22 Carlos Nguyen: Yes, we offer dedicated pools per region; the Private control plane can be configured to restrict data residency. There's a small infra setup lead time — usually 2-3 weeks for EU provisioning if you accept standard networking. If you need air-gapped or customer-managed HSM there is extra time.
02:43 Liam O'Connor: Good to know. Procurement question: will pricing change per region? We want to avoid surprises.
02:50 Maya Thompson: Regions are priced similarly but there are differences due to infra costs; we'll include a region addendum in the pricing doc. For a 24-month commitment we can provide a better unit rate and an allocation for burst capacity at reduced incremental cost.
03:05 Jared Kim: For legal — last renewal we had a few redlines around data destruction and audit logs, Redwood's standard SLA looked fine, but we need SOC 2 artifacts and clarity on KMS integrations.
03:18 Maya Thompson: Absolutely. I'll share SOC 2 report, SOC 2 cover letter, and our network/arch diagram today. We support customer-managed KMS via standard KMS or HSM integrations in Private. Carlos can follow up on the KMS flow.
03:32 Carlos Nguyen: For KMS we support both bring-your-own key and Redwood-managed rotation. If you go with BYOK, the keys never leave your tenant; we log all envelope decryption events in audit logs accessible via the Console.
03:45 Priya Rao: Are audit logs immutable? We need tamper evidence.
03:48 Carlos Nguyen: Yes we write logs to append-only storage and you can forward to your SIEM; we also support write-once WORM buckets if you need that.
03:58 Maya Thompson: Great. On the benchmark — Carlos, you mentioned running the 8xA100 baseline with our sample. What's the timeline and what do you need from Cascade?
04:06 Carlos Nguyen: We'll need the sample payloads and a short runbook for traffic shape. Ideally a 24-hour run to capture spikes and steady-state. We can start as soon as they share the sample traces and a test key. Deliverables: raw perf numbers, token/sec, p95/p99 latency, and cost-per-1000 tokens estimate on the proposed config. I'll include a comparison to your current setup.
04:30 Liam O'Connor: We can get that over by Monday. Procurement is also going to push for a PO around the 14th. Can we have pricing documented by then?
04:39 Maya Thompson: Yes — I'll push the addendum tomorrow and include both 12- and 24-month pricing. For 24-month we can offer a 12% discount off list and a committed burst bucket.
04:51 Jared Kim: For contract term — does the 24-month lock regional add? We want flexibility to add regions mid-term.
04:59 Maya Thompson: You can add regions mid-term; we'll prorate capacity and apply the committed rate to the committed baseline. We'll put the mechanics in the addendum so your legal team has clarity.
05:12 Priya Rao: A few technical Qs: how does rollback/fallback work if EU region capacity is saturated? We need graceful degradation.
05:21 Carlos Nguyen: We support smart routing with failover policies — you can set per-route policies to fall back to a nearby region or to a lower-cost model variant. For regulated traffic you can set a hard constraint to never leave the EU. For non-regulated, fallback is allowed and we route by lowest-latency compatible variant.
05:42 Sara Martinez: Any limits on model variants for Dedicated? We run a custom quantized variant in staging.
05:48 Carlos Nguyen: We can serve custom quantized builds; there's a model-onboarding checklist. For custom kernels we'll need to validate compatibility; that typically adds one week to the onboarding timeline.
06:00 Maya Thompson: Okay timeline recap: Carlos runs benchmark after samples Monday, Maya sends pricing and SOC2 docs today/tomorrow, Cascade confirms region list and procurement timeline by next Thursday. Legal call week of Dec 14. Does that align?
06:15 Liam O'Connor: Yes aligns. One ask — can you include an explicit line item for the burst buffer in the pricing so procurement can see the capex/opex split?
06:23 Maya Thompson: Will do. We'll call that out as a reserved burst bucket with a capped per-minute spend.
06:30 Jared Kim: Also, can you include cancellation terms and termination assistance in the addendum? Last time it was a bit sparse.
06:36 Maya Thompson: Yes, we'll include termination assistance — data export windows, handover support.
06:42 Carlos Nguyen: One more technical note — depending on your context lengths we may recommend a quantized 4-bit profile for steady-state to save cost; we'll show cost vs latency trade-offs in the benchmark.
06:55 Priya Rao: That would help.
07:00 Maya Thompson: Awesome. Any other blockers?
07:03 Sara Martinez: None from engineering.
07:05 Liam O'Connor: No.
07:07 Maya Thompson: Great thanks everyone — we'll follow up with notes and the addendum. Talk soon.

Action recap (verbatim): Maya to send SOC 2 & pricing addendum; Carlos to run 24-hour benchmark; Cascade to confirm EU region list and PO timing; procurement to send redlines.

References shared during call: link: /redwood/docs/soc2-2026, link: /redwood/benchmarks/ce-sample-report, note: pricing addendum draft (to be attached).

End of transcript.
